# Draft:Jaipur Centre of Culture and Arts

The Jaipur Centre of Culture and Arts (JCCA) is a contemporary art gallery and cultural centre located in Jaipur, Rajasthan, India. It was established in 2023. The institution was established to present exhibitions of modern and contemporary Indian art. Since its opening, it has organised a series of exhibitions featuring artists associated with modern and contemporary art in India.
History
The Jaipur Centre of Culture and Arts (JCCA) was established in 2023 as an exhibition space for modern and contemporary Indian art. The centre is located in a four-storey building in Jaipur that includes gallery spaces, a café, and an area referred to as a "Culture Hub". The facility is used for exhibitions and related cultural activities associated with the gallery's programming.
In 2023, the centre presented Under the Mask, an exhibition of works by sculptor and painter Himmat Shah. The exhibition included a series of drawings created during the COVID-19 pandemic. The gallery also presented Forms and Myths, an exhibition of paintings by artist Manu Parekh.
Other exhibitions organised by the centre have included Art of Bengal, which featured works by artists associated with the Bengal art tradition, and Blooming Thar, which presented works by contemporary artists from Rajasthan. In January 2025, the gallery presented The Color Montage, a group exhibition featuring works in multiple visual media.
In September 2025, JCCA opened A Prelude to Wounds – Unseen Somnath Hore. The exhibition presented drawings, prints, and sculptures by the modernist artist Somnath Hore, including works originally created in the winter of 1966–67 that later informed his Wounds series.
